specification.objective: Add safe, reviewable cleanup for local branches merged by commit reachability into a selected base, with CLI and TUI workflows.

requirements.statement: Resolve the cleanup base to a commit OID and identify only local branch tips reachable from that commit; default to current HEAD.
Protect the current branch and selected base branch from cleanup.
Support repeatable filtering by configured upstream remote names; include branches whose resolved upstream remote is in the selected set, without fetching.
Provide a preview-first cleanup CLI and require explicit --yes before batch deletion.
Revalidate eligibility per selected branch and delete only with safe git branch -d semantics.

Provide a TUI cleanup modal with individual/mass selection, a warning, explicit confirmation, and cancellation; keep the selected candidate visible and allow navigation through long or wrapped review content in a bounded viewport.
Report per-branch outcomes with navigation through long reports and refresh TUI state after batch attempts, including partial failures.
Never fetch, prune, push, or delete remote branches as an implicit cleanup effect.
Document CLI/TUI behavior, customization, safety semantics, examples, and ancestry limitations.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Candidates are local branches reachable from the resolved base; current/base and unmerged branches are excluded.
Exact exclusions and repeatable upstream-remote filters change the candidate set as specified; branches from any selected remote are included and other remotes are excluded without network activity.
CLI invocation reviews candidates by default and deletes only after --yes.
Batch deletion revalidates eligibility and preserves Git's safe refusal for unmerged work.
TUI users can open cleanup, select candidates, select all/none, keep the selected candidate visible, review a warning, confirm, or cancel.
TUI cleanup reports partial outcomes, allows access to every report detail, and refreshes repository state after the attempt.
README examples and safety/ancestry limitations match implemented CLI and TUI behavior.
Candidates, confirmation branches, and report details remain accessible by scrolling when their content exceeds a small viewport or wraps across lines.

invariants.statement: Repository branch names are passed as argv data and are never interpolated into a shell command.
Cleanup mutates local refs only and never uses force deletion.
CLI and TUI use the same candidate and revalidation rules.

forbidden_states.statement: The checked-out branch or selected base branch is deleted by cleanup.
An unmerged branch is force-deleted or removed because of a stale candidate list.
Cleanup performs implicit fetch, prune, push, or remote-ref deletion.

inputs.statement: Optional base ref, exact excluded branch names, zero or more upstream remote names, selected candidate names, and CLI confirmation flag.
Local Git refs and configured upstream metadata from the current repository snapshot.

outputs.statement: Resolved base, ordered candidate list, preview/deletion feedback, and per-branch deleted/skipped/failed outcomes.
Refreshed TUI repository snapshot after a batch cleanup attempt.

failure_semantics.statement: An invalid repository or base returns an error before mutation.
A branch no longer eligible at deletion time is skipped or fails safely; other selected branches may succeed and every outcome is reported.
No-candidate preview reports zero candidates and performs no mutation.
